lectures.name: Abortion in Canada
lectures.title: Abortion in Canada
lectures.framing: Gestational age chooses the method, and the method chooses the risks. Everything below 12 weeks can go medical or surgical; above it the options narrow and the complication profile changes. 98% of abortions are uncomplicated.
lectures.keypoints: the 70-day / 10-week / 14-week / 25-week ladder is the spine of this lecture. Cervical shock is vasovagal at the paracervical block, not haemorrhage. Asherman syndrome risk is 8% after one curettage and up to 30% after a third within 24 hours — and trauma, not infection, is the major cause. dilation & evacuation is the safest 2nd-trimester method, and the limiting factor in Canada is the shrinking number of trained practitioners.

blocks.html: Mechanism. mifepristone blocks the progesterone receptor → decidual necrosis + cervical ripening → rhythmic contractions → detachment → expulsion; contractions peak at 36-48 h. misoprostol (prostaglandin E1) works down two arms — ↓ collagen → ↑ matrix metalloproteinases → cervical ripening, and inhibits adenyl cyclase → ↓ cyclic adenosine monophosphate → ↑ calcium → ↑ uterine tone. methotrexate blocks dihydrofolate reductase, acting on cytotrophoblast, not the embryo, and is teratogenic.

blocks.html:
Workup skeleton

- History/Physical exam — no referral needed, most clinics self-refer · gestational age by ultrasound · medical/surgical history · Rh status · consent · counselling

- Investigations — ⚠ beta human chorionic gonadotropin follow-up after medical abortion: ↓ 50% by day 3 or ↓ 80% by days 7-14 = success; a plateau = failure

- Treatment of failure — > 50% abort with a second 800 mcg misoprostol; < 5% need surgical evacuation

- Follow-up — appointment within 11 days; ⭐ ovulation returns 2 weeks after a 1st-trimester abortion, so contraception starts immediately — same-day intrauterine device, implant or DepoProvera, or tubal interruption if done under GA
Dilatation required = the number of weeks of gestation. Hegar dilators; skipping mechanical dilation ↓ discomfort and ↓ infection when cervical prep is adequate.

lectures.name: Fertilization & Infertility
lectures.title: Fertilization and Infertility
lectures.framing: Infertility is 50% female and 50% male, so both partners are investigated. The workup is six steps timed to the cycle, and each step answers one question: is the brain signalling? is the cavity and are the tubes open? did she ovulate? are the sperm adequate?
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ primary infertility means she has never been PREGNANT — not that she has no children, and a partner's children from another relationship do not change it. AMH measures reserve and does NOT predict natural fertility. Male aging ↓ volume, motility and morphology but leaves sperm concentration stable, and is NOT associated with aneuploidy — that is the maternal-age effect. Recurrent pregnancy loss is ≥ 2 losses, consecutive or not, including biochemical, and ~50% stay unexplained; the treatable one is antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (5-20%), treated with heparin + aspirin at the first positive test.

blocks.html: Ordering estradiol, LH and FSH together is the point. An FSH of 30 alone reads as diminished reserve — but if estradiol is also 500 she is not on day 2, and that FSH may be normal. LH is checked early because it should be low; in PCOS baseline LH can be 18, which is why ovulation strips fail in PCOS.

blocks.html: AMH: > 28 suggests PCOS · 15-28 normal · < 15 diminished reserve. It guides in vitro fertilization dosing, not natural-fertility counselling.

Confirming ovulation: mid-luteal progesterone · urine LH — a true surge is both lines equally dark, and ovulation follows in ~36 h · ultrasound (needs daily scans) · cervical mucus, 2 consecutive clear stretchy days · basal body temperature.

Irregular cycle by time since menarche: first year — normal · after 1 year — > 90 days is abnormal · 3 years to perimenopause — < 21 days, > 35 days, or < 8 cycles a year. Primary amenorrhea: no menarche by 15, or > 3 years after thelarche.

Male factors, in order: idiopathic (commonest) · varicocele (2nd) · exogenous steroids · erectile/ejaculatory dysfunction · infections · genetic (Klinefelter syndrome, Y microdeletions) · radiation/chemo · lifestyle — marijuana, smoking, hot tubs.

lectures.name: Contraception
lectures.title: Contraception and drugs used in gynecology
lectures.framing: Two questions, in this order. First, which axis is this drug on — estrogen, progestin, or androgen — because the indication and the adverse effects both follow from it. Then, for contraception specifically, counsel from the TYPICAL-use column, never the perfect-use one. Failure rates below are pregnancies per 1000 women per year of typical use.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The progestin-only contraceptive's primary mechanism is LOCAL, not central — cervical mucus, tubal peristalsis and endometrium, with ovulation suppressed in only ~50% of cycles (the injection excepted), which is exactly why the mini-pill fails at 3 hours late while a combined pill forgives. Estrogen and progestin oppose each other on the endometrium but are synergic on the breast — the one risk adding a progestin does not fix. Combined methods are contraindicated over age 35 at more than 15 cigarettes per day, and a past deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism contraindicates them only when she is off anticoagulation AND at higher risk of recurrence. tamoxifen is the selective estrogen receptor modulator that raises endometrial cancer risk; raloxifene is not — both raise VTE. clomiphene raises gonadotropins by blocking central negative feedback, which is why an estrogen receptor antagonist induces ovulation.

lectures.framing: Every agent here does one of three things: disrupt the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, block the overgrowth of a sex-hormone-dependent tissue, or replace a hormone that is absent. Work out which, and the indications and adverse effects follow from it.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The progestin-only contraceptive's primary mechanism is local, not central — that is the single most-tested fact here, and it is what makes adherence matter so much more for the mini-pill. Every contraindication in the combined column is an ESTROGEN contraindication — which is why the answer to “what can she have instead?” is almost always a progestin-only or intrauterine method. migraine with aura and an acute thromboembolic event are category ④ for combined methods only; hypertension crosses from relative to absolute at ≥ 160 systolic or ≥ 100 diastolic. The patch and the ring bypass first-pass metabolism, and that — not the dose — is why they carry more VTE risk than the pill. Drospirenone is the anti-androgenic progestin (spironolactone-derived) — the one to reach for in hormonal acne, and the one that risks hyperkalemia; estranes and gonanes are androgenic instead. Ulipristal beats levonorgestrel at every interval, including inside 72 hours ⚠ — an Elentra module question keys this the other way, and the lecture's own meta-analysis slide is the one to trust. GnRH agonists flare before they suppress; antagonists never flare. Finasteride lowers dihydrotestosterone, it does not block the androgen receptor — which is why it shrinks a prostate and thins body hair without touching muscle mass. ⚠ No emergency contraceptive works once implantation has happened — only mifepristone acts on an established pregnancy.

lectures.name: Vaginal Discharge
lectures.title: Vaginal Discharge
lectures.framing: pH is the first discriminator and it splits the four diagnoses in half. estrogen drives discharge containing glycogen, which feeds lactobacilli and holds the pH acidic — so a pH above 4.5 means the flora has already changed.
lectures.keypoints: Know the ranking, the symptoms and the diagnostic test; for treatment know the route, not the dose. Trichomonas coexists with BV in 60%; 20% of women culture positive for Candida while asymptomatic, which is why it is treated only when symptomatic. lectures.name: Cervical Cancer Screening
lectures.title: Cervical Cancer Screening
lectures.framing: Screening works because the precursor lasts years. Most human papillomavirus (HPV) infections clear; some produce a squamous intraepithelial lesion; a few progress to carcinoma, usually after 10+ years. Treat the lesion and the cancer never happens — which is why cervical cancer is 16th in Canada and 4th worldwide.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ eligibility is any ASYMPTOMATIC person with a cervix who has EVER been sexually active, from about age 25 — screening is not for symptomatic people, and a never-sexually-active patient may defer. Vaccination does not replace screening. At least 75% of people are exposed to HPV in a lifetime and condoms are only partially protective, because transmission is skin-to-skin beyond what a condom covers. In Ontario non-invasive prenatal testing-style logic does not apply here: primary HPV screening is the direction of travel, but the sample must still include the transformation zone. ⚠ An LSIL alone does not tell you which strain caused it — which is why the strain matters more than the grade.

Vaccines: Cervarix (16, 18) · Gardasil (16, 18, 6, 11) · Gardasil-9 (those plus 31, 33, 45, 52, 58). England has almost eliminated cervical cancer in women born since 1 September 1995, most in those vaccinated at 12-13.

Sample collection — what gets a specimen rejected: know the system — ThinPrep: do NOT leave the device in the vial; SurePath: it may be left · lukewarm water for the speculum, and gel only if water-based and sparing · full legal name, date of birth, collection date · check the vial expiry.

Self-sampling. She collects her own vaginal sample; it holds mostly vaginal cells and only rare cervical cells, and HPV testing still works purely because the test is that sensitive. It exists to reach the under- and never-screened. Australia offers it to all screen-eligible people since 2022; British Columbia to specific populations. Equivalence to provider sampling is cautious optimism, not settled.

lectures.framing: This lecture is about the population, not the patient. The clinical question is who has an infection; the public-health question is what makes a disease reportable, and what does reporting buy.
lectures.keypoints: the list of risk factors is broad enough that most sexually active people meet at least one — which is the argument for offering testing rather than selecting for it. ⭐ Reportability is what makes contact tracing possible, so it is not an administrative detail but the mechanism by which a diagnosed infection stops spreading. 48% of abortions worldwide are unsafe and 97% of those are in developing countries — the same inequity shapes the STI burden.

Risk factors, grouped by what they actually describe

- Partner — sexual contact with a known STI · a new partner, or more than two in the past year · a serially monogamous pattern, since these individuals are less likely to be tested · anonymous partnering (internet, bathhouse, rave)

- Age — ⭐ sexually active youth under 25, in whom chlamydia and gonorrhea are especially concentrated

- Contraception — none, or sole use of a non-barrier method: oral contraceptives, Depo Provera and the intrauterine device all count, because none is a barrier

- Substances — injection drug use · alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, ecstasy, crystal meth, especially when associated with sex

- Practices — unprotected oral, genital or anal sex · sex with blood exchange, including sadomasochism · sharing sex toys

- Circumstance — sex workers and clients · "survival sex", exchanging sex for money, drugs, shelter or food · street involvement and homelessness · victims of sexual assault or abuse

- History — a previous STI

- ⚠ Chlamydia and gonorrhea are reportable — trace and treat contacts, and advise no sexual contact until both partners are treated

lectures.framing: Two questions run this lecture: is the pregnancy inside the uterus, and is it viable? A positive beta human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) with pain or bleeding is an ectopic pregnancy until the ultrasound says otherwise, and the ultrasound is only interpretable against the β-hCG level.
lectures.keypoints: β-hCG is the most important predictor of methotrexate failure — 92% success below 5000, and 4x the failure rate above it. Half of miscarriages have a normal karyotype; of the abnormal half, trisomy 16 is commonest and always lethal, and XO is the commonest isolated aneuploidy. Cerclage is elective at 12-16 weeks and rescue below 23 weeks.

Sites: tube 80% — ampulla 70%, isthmus 12%, fimbria 6% — interstitial 2%, ovarian 0.5-3%, cervical < 0.1%, abdominal and cesarean section scar 1 in 2000, heterotopic 1 in 30,000 but 1% with assisted reproductive technology. ⚠ This deck says 2% of pregnancies and 80% tubal; the acute pelvic pain deck says 6-16% and 98% tubal.

Workup skeleton

- History and physical exam — the triad is abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding and a positive β-hCG; then displaced or enlarged uterus, orthostatic hypotension, pelvic mass, bulging fornix, cervical motion tenderness, shoulder pain from diaphragmatic irritation

- Investigations — β-hCG doubles every 1.4-2.1 days, and 85% of viable intrauterine pregnancies (IUPs) rise ≥ 66% in 48 hours · complete blood count, group and screen · transvaginal ultrasound should see an IUP above a β-hCG of 1500, and 99% by 3150 (transabdominal needs 6500) · "ring of fire" · free fluid

- Treatment — expectant if β-hCG declining and < 200, mass < 3.5 cm, no rupture, asymptomatic · methotrexate 50 mg/m² intramuscular ⚠ not mg/kg · surgery for instability, rupture, methotrexate contraindication

- ⭐ Any Rh-negative patient with a positive β-hCG and vaginal bleeding needs Rh immunoglobulin — WinRho or Rhogam — to protect her future pregnancies

lectures.name: Endometriosis
lectures.title: Endometriosis
lectures.framing: Endometrial tissue outside the uterine cavity, and the disease does not behave the way its extent predicts. ⭐ The severity of disease does not correlate with the degree of pain, and the examination is often normal — which is why it takes years to diagnose.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ most women with endometriosis do NOT experience infertility, despite it being the headline complication. Pain begins about 2 days BEFORE menses — which is what separates it from primary dysmenorrhea, where pain comes with the bleeding. Many patients have had YEARS without a diagnosis, told repeatedly that painful periods are normal in the teenage years.

blocks.html: Two ways to suppress ovulation, and the split is the discriminator. Pseudopregnancy — flood it with progestin: oral contraceptive pill, NuvaRing, Evra patch, Depo Provera, hormonal intrauterine system, Visanne. Pseudomenopause — withdraw the estrogen: danazol, a testosterone derivative, and Lupron or Zoladex, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists.

Why it causes infertility — four separate mechanisms: embryotoxic factors in the peritoneal fluid · lower implantation rates · impaired follicle development with diminished reserve · impaired tubal transport from a chronically pro-inflammatory pelvis.

Diagnosis. Gold standard is laparoscopy with biopsy, and the pathologist needs ⭐ any 2 of 3: endometrial glands or epithelium, endometrial stroma, and hemosiderin. Early lesions are "blueberry"; late ones are "powder burns" with adhesions, and ⚠ late disease burns out — no endometrial tissue remains, so a negative late biopsy does not exclude it. Because not everyone can be scoped, most diagnoses rest on symptoms and response to medical therapy.

Staging uses the revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine classification — I-II minimal/mild, superficial plaques without significant adhesions; III-IV moderate/severe, ovarian involvement, deep disease, dense adhesions, kissing ovaries, a frozen pelvis.

Dyspareunia — ask, because she will not raise it. "Have you ever had penetrative sexual activity? If yes, do you experience pain with it?" Maintain a non-judgmental, normalizing approach. Superficial pain on penetration points to vulvodynia, atrophy, vulvar skin conditions or vaginismus; deep pain points to endometriosis, masses, adhesions or musculoskeletal causes.

That is a denominator effect, not a risk. A ruptured cyst mimics a ruptured ectopic exactly, and only the β-hCG separates them. Significant haemorrhage from a ruptured cyst is uncommon — most bleed minimally, which is why instability is notable.

lectures.keypoints: ⭐ up to 50% of women with chronic pelvic pain have experienced some kind of abuse or trauma — take the history. Boggy distinguishes adenomyosis from the firm irregular uterus of fibroids. Pain with no cyclic pattern and a normal structural examination is myofascial, and the honest goal there is pain reduction and improved function, not cure.

blocks.html: Why NSAIDs are first line in dysmenorrhea. Menses is a generalized inflammatory state: prostaglandins from endometrial sloughing induce contractions → uterine pressure exceeds arterial pressure → uterine ischaemia → anaerobic metabolites accumulate → stimulate type C pain neurons. Any hormonal method that reduces menstrual flow improves it, because there is less endometrium to slough.

Fibroids — location decides everything. More common in African American, obese, early menarche and hereditary cases; ⭐ smoking is associated with LESS risk. Submucosal → bleeding and hysteroscopic resection · intramural and subserosal → uterine artery embolization · pedunculated → risk of torsion, and myomectomy or hysterectomy. Reproductive dysfunction only occurs with fibroids that distort the cavity. ⚠ Pregnancy after uterine artery embolization is NOT advised — case reports only, which is what separates UAE from myomectomy for a patient who still wants to conceive.

Chronic pelvic pain accounts for 10% of outpatient gynecology referrals, 40% of laparoscopies and 20% of hysterectomies for benign disease.

lectures.name: Genetic Screening for Pregnancy in Canada
lectures.title: Genetic Screening for Pregnancy in Canada
lectures.framing: Primary prevention happens before conception; secondary prevention happens after it. ⭐ Every couple has a 2-3% chance of a baby with some congenital anomaly regardless of screening — that baseline never reaches zero, and every result is interpreted against it.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ in Ontario NIPT is NOT recommended as a first-line screen for low-risk women, despite being the best performer in the table — which is why the funded indications (previous trisomy, maternal age 40+, NT > 3.5 mm, positive eFTS) exist. A positive screen always needs a diagnostic test. Cytology of the family matters: when a fetal aneuploidy proves translocation-derived, karyotype the parents — a daughter has a 50% chance of carrying it and the carrier's siblings need counselling too.

blocks.html: Fragile X — three triggers to refer: a personal or family history · ⭐ ovarian insufficiency with elevated follicle-stimulating hormone before 40, of unknown cause · ⭐ male relatives with isolated cerebellar ataxia and tremor. The 50-200 premutation causes fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (often misdiagnosed as Parkinsonism) or primary ovarian insufficiency — see FMR1 disorders.

Nuchal translucency > 3.5 mm raises the risk of aneuploidy (21, 13, 18, 45X), congenital heart defect, skeletal dysplasia and Noonan syndrome. ⚠ Turner is 45,X with streak ovaries and a webbed neck; Noonan overlaps physically but has a NORMAL karyotype, affects BOTH sexes, is autosomal dominant, and risks cardiomyopathy — which is why the karyotype that settles Turner is the test that misses Noonan.

Timelines are the real constraint, against a 24-week limit on termination: NIPT ~10 days · CVS microarray ~2 weeks · single gene test ~3 weeks minimum. ⚠ "Lethal" does not necessarily mean the baby dies immediately after birth — technology can sustain life for indefinite periods.

Preimplantation genetic testing requires in vitro fertilization with or without intracytoplasmic sperm injection, embryo biopsy and selected transfer. DNA comes from polar bodies, one blastomere from a cleavage-stage embryo, or 5-10 trophectoderm cells from a blastocyst. Tested by polymerase chain reaction for single genes and fluorescence in situ hybridization for translocations and de novo aneuploidy. Not covered by the Ontario Health Insurance Plan.

lectures.name: In-Class - Amenorrhea
lectures.title: Approach to Amenorrhea
lectures.framing: Amenorrhea is a compartment problem — the block sits in the outflow tract, the ovary, the pituitary or the hypothalamus — and two numbers sort it: the beta hCG first, always, then follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which says whether the pituitary is shouting at a dead ovary (high FSH) or not shouting at all (low FSH).
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ rule out pregnancy first, before any other test and whatever the story sounds like. High FSH means the ovary has failed; low FSH means the problem is above it — that one number splits the differential, and a normal FSH with normal prolactin and TSH points at anovulation, which is where PCOS lives. PCOS is the commonest secondary cause (28%), Turner the commonest primary (27%). ⚠ The workbook keys primary amenorrhea as "no periods by 16"; the lecture uses 13 without and 15 with secondary sex characteristics — answer to the source in front of you.

lectures.name: Hysterectomy Approaches

lectures.framing: Choose the least invasive route the anatomy allows. Every approach is a "short stay" with same-day discharge except abdominal, and the whole lecture is a ladder: vaginal → laparoscopic-assisted vaginal hysterectomy (LAVH) → total laparoscopic hysterectomy (TLH) or robotic → abdominal, where each rung is what to use when the one above is blocked. ⚠ When the indication is bleeding control, medical options come first - hysterectomy is for failed medical management and special circumstances.

Vaginal is the only approach without abdominal entry, and the one that cannot get at tubes and ovaries. Shared limitation of every minimally invasive route is a large uterus; the vaginal-route pair add narrow introitus/pelvis and poor uterine descent, and the laparoscopic pair add suturing skill and operative time. lectures.framing: One procedure, one objective: know what goes wrong and what you do about it. A dilation and curettage (D&C) is vacuum aspiration of a pregnancy under 14 weeks through a rigid cannula on electric suction; every complication is a consequence of one step, so learn the complications by the step that causes them.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Antibiotic prophylaxis is indicated for therapeutic abortion but NOT for a D&C done for missed abortion or pregnancy loss - the same procedure, two indications, one gets antibiotics. ⚠ Asherman's follows curettage in 8%, and repeat curettage (for retained products or retained placenta post partum) raises it to 30% by a third consecutive procedure - which is why retained products are managed with misoprostol where possible rather than a reflex second D&C. Hematometra is re-evacuated immediately; retained products may wait for medical management - the two "something is still in the uterus" complications get opposite tempos.

lectures.name: Clinical Approach to Menopause
lectures.title: Clinical approach to menopause
lectures.framing: Every treatment decision splits on which symptom you are treating: vasomotor symptoms (VMS) are systemic and need systemic therapy; genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is local and is treated locally. Estrogen is the gold standard for VMS and the second line for GSM, so the real question is whether she can have it systemically: no contraindications, younger than 60, and < 10 years post menopause.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Estrogen is the gold standard for VMS, and a woman with a uterus must have progesterone with it; estrogen alone only after hysterectomy. Vaginal estrogen treats GSM but not VMS, and systemic MHT can under-treat GSM, so some women need both. Transdermal estrogen skips first-pass metabolism and has the better clotting profile. After menopause estradiol and progesterone fall while follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone rise (loss of feedback). A history of venous thromboembolism or stroke is enough to contraindicate estrogen - it need not be active.

blocks.lead:

lectures.framing: Every ovarian tumour is named by its lineage (epithelial, germ cell, sex cord/stromal) plus its behaviour (benign, borderline, malignant), and the age of the patient predicts the lineage: epithelial in adults, germ cell in the young. lectures.title: Pathology of the breast
lectures.framing: Place the lesion by the tissue it arises from, then tell the lesions of that tissue apart by presentation. The terminal duct lobular unit (TDLU) grows fibrocystic change and carcinoma (in situ and invasive); the large ducts and nipple grow papillomas, duct ectasia, mastitis and Paget's; the intralobular stroma grows fibroadenoma and phyllodes; the interlobular stroma and fat grow fat necrosis, pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia and mesenchymal tumours.

lectures.framing: Three providers, one team. The chart turns on who can do what, and at which point a pregnancy leaves their scope: family medicine and midwives each carry a low-risk pregnancy from antenatal care to 6 weeks post partum, while the obstetrician is the consultant for anything complicated and the only one who operates.

Preeclampsia is a consult trigger in all three phases, and the post partum list is short: postpartum hemorrhage, a 3rd or 4th degree tear, preeclampsia. Asking for help is not a failure.

lectures.framing: A teratogen is judged by what it hits and when: the same exposure does nothing in weeks 1-2, produces a major structural anomaly during organogenesis (weeks 3-8), and a functional or minor defect in the fetal period. 9 in 10 pregnant women take at least one medication, so the question is rarely whether she is exposed but how to counsel her.

lectures.name: Approach to First Trimester Bleeding & Ultrasound
lectures.title: First trimester ultrasound and hCG
lectures.framing: Two questions, one for each half of the lecture. For dating: which landmark is visible decides which measurement dates the pregnancy, and each landmark is retired the moment the next one appears. For a positive test with an empty uterus: a single human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) value never settles a pregnancy of unknown location; only the rate of change does, so the answer is almost always to repeat it.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Once an embryo is seen, MSD is never used again: CRL dates the pregnancy, best when > 10 mm (7 weeks), accurate to 3-8 days. A gestational sac is visible from 32 days, a yolk sac from 5 to 5+5 weeks, a heartbeat by 6+0. hCG level does not predict ectopic rupture, and a falling hCG does not exclude an ectopic: 8% of untreated ectopics fall at the same rate as a miscarriage (Silva 2006). All women should be offered a dating scan at 7-12 weeks; it beats LMP and cuts inductions for post-dates.

blocks.html:
Workup skeleton

- History - last menstrual period (LMP) dating assumes regular 28-day cycles, mid-cycle ovulation and fertilization, correct recall, off the oral contraceptive pill for months; even a correct LMP cannot fix implantation without assisted reproductive technology (follicular waves · sperm survive 5-7 days · ovulation-to-implantation varies by up to 11 days)

- Investigations - transvaginal ultrasound (TVUS) of uterus and adnexa is the quality standard, transabdominal only for a high mass or free fluid · serial hCG rather than one absolute value · ⚠ a single hCG in the overlap zone does not distinguish viable IUP, NVIUP and ectopic

- Treatment - stable + hCG 2000-3000 + no ectopic seen → repeat, do not act; this spares inappropriate misoprostol, dilation and curettage and laparoscopy

- Follow-up - a pregnancy is resolved only below 5 mIU/mL · ⚠ a resolving ectopic can still rupture while its hCG falls · rupture under close surveillance: 0.03% of all PUL, 1.7% of diagnosed ectopics

lectures.name: Hypertension in Pregnancy
lectures.title: Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy
lectures.framing: Every decision turns on two questions: when did the blood pressure (BP) rise relative to 20 weeks, and is the high BP the disease itself (chronic / gestational) or a symptom of it (pre-eclampsia / eclampsia)? The first sets the diagnosis; the second sets whether you treat the number or deliver the patient.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ 20 weeks is the line: HTN diagnosed before it is chronic, after it (with normal BPs documented) is gestational; pre-eclampsia adds proteinuria. Mild is >140 / >90, severe is >160 / >110, always 2 readings >15 min apart. ⚠ HELLP can present with a completely normal BP. The primary maternal danger of severe HTN is stroke, so any neurological symptom means investigate for an intracranial event. Treat the number in chronic / gestational HTN; in pre-eclampsia the number is a symptom and complications drive delivery planning.

- Physical exam: 2 readings >15 min apart, seated, calm, correct cuff size · exclude white-coat and pain-driven elevation · neuro symptoms ⇒ rule out an intracranial event

- Investigations: urine protein · platelets, white blood cell count, international normalized ratio (INR), partial thromboplastin time · creatinine, uric acid · liver function tests (LFTs), albumin · oxygen saturation · fetal: growth, amniotic fluid, umbilical artery end-diastolic flow

- Follow-up: complications decide delivery planning · MgSO4 continues 12-48 h post-partum

lectures.name: Topics of Antenatal Care
lectures.title: Topics in antenatal care
lectures.framing: Three routine pieces of antenatal care, each with a when and a why: feed the pregnancy (folate + iron), vaccinate it (inactivated only), and screen the mother's blood. The antibody question turns on one thing: does she already have an antibody? If not, Rh immunoglobulin (RhIG) prevents one; if so, the titre decides whether the fetus is watched.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The only vaccine category not considered safe is live attenuated (measles-mumps-rubella, varicella, bacille Calmette-Guérin), and the reason is a theoretical one, not an observed one. Tdap is timed (27-32 weeks) because the point is the baby's passive immunity; influenza is not timed because the point is the mother. RhIG is prophylaxis for the unsensitized: it clears fetal cells before the maternal immune system responds, so it does nothing once an antibody exists. ⚠ A titre of 1/8 or greater is the line for severe-anemia risk; below it, keep testing monthly. Sensitization needs a source: previous pregnancy, transfusion, or drug abuse (module Q94), and the fetus is only at risk if it carries the antigen, hence the partner screen.

lectures.name: Care for Pregnancy in the First Trimester
lectures.title: Care for pregnancy in the first trimester
lectures.framing: Three jobs in the first 12 weeks: confirm the pregnancy, date it, and screen it. Every question turns on a threshold or a counting rule, and the one rule above the rest: once the estimated date of birth (EDB) is set by the most reliable method (in vitro fertilization (IVF) transfer date, or 1st-trimester ultrasound) it is FIXED - a later scan that disagrees is reporting growth, not a new due date.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ EDB is fixed once set by the most reliable method - later discrepancies are growth, not dating. ⚠ Early symptoms should never be relied on exclusively; some have none, some are misattributed (the flu). ⚠ Bleeding in early pregnancy is mistaken for menses and delays diagnosis, especially at the extremes of age and on the oral contraceptive pill. A gestational sac alone does not confirm a pregnancy - the yolk sac is required, and location must be established to exclude ectopic. CRL after 14 weeks is not a dating tool. lectures.title: Approach to sexual health
lectures.framing: Two halves to this lecture: the physiology you contrast between cis-men and cis-women, and the interview you run so the patient can raise the problem they came in with. The whole conversation turns on one move: acknowledge your own implicit biases before you walk into the room, then ask permission to talk about sexual health, so the patient never has to raise it first.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ The refractory period is the sex difference: males are physiologically incapable of another orgasm after the first; females have none and can have multiple orgasms. NO is the neurotransmitter of clitoral engorgement, and photoplethysmography is how VBV is measured. Orgasm is cerebral, not spinal. The interview separates on repetition as the tool that unpacks a euphemism, and on asking permission first. ⚠ Never assume orientation or monogamy in the wording: "How many partners in the past year?", not "Are you monogamous?"; say "partner".

lectures.name: Antepartum Hemorrhage & Abnormal Placentation
lectures.title: Antepartum hemorrhage
lectures.framing: Bleeding in the 2nd/3rd trimester turns on two questions: is it painful, and whose blood is it? A painful bleed with a tender uterus is an abruption, a painless bleed is a previa until the ultrasound says otherwise, and a small bleed with a distressed fetus is fetal blood - a vasa previa. Whatever the cause, assess mother and fetus together, continuously, and remember that ongoing bleeding depletes clotting factors at the placental interface.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Painful bleeding + tender uterus = abruption; painless bleeding = previa; small bleed + fetal distress = vasa previa, and the blood is fetal. ⚠ Never examine the cervix of a bleeder until ultrasound has cleared the placenta. Kleihaur-Betke finds fetal blood in the mother; Apt finds it in the vaginal blood - only Apt diagnoses vasa previa. Abruption is a diagnosis of exclusion; previa is an ultrasound diagnosis. A previous C/S raises the risk of previa and accreta, not vasa previa; vasa previa comes from a velamentous cord (type 1) or a succenturiate lobe (type 2).

blocks.html:
Workup skeleton

- History: previous bleeding this pregnancy · previous abruption · trauma (motor vehicle collision, fall) · hypertension, autoimmune disease · smoking/cocaine · previous C/S or uterine surgery (accreta) · placental location on the anatomy scan

- Physical exam: maternal vitals · abdominal exam for uterine tenderness/rigidity and fetal presentation · speculum for the source · ⚠ no cervical examination until ultrasound has shown the placenta is clear of the cervix - examining a previa can precipitate massive hemorrhage

- Investigations: stat complete blood count (baseline hemoglobin, platelets) · international normalized ratio / partial thromboplastin time / fibrinogen (coagulopathy) · creatinine · with or without liver function tests (rule out pre-eclampsia, acute liver injury) · group and screen · Kleihaur-Betke test = fetal blood in the maternal circulation (trauma, abruption) · Apt test = fetal blood in the vaginal bleed (vasa previa) · ultrasound for placental location

- Treatment / Management: active bleed + preterm: birthing unit, continuous fetal monitoring, steroids for lungs, magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, neonatal intensive care unit / tertiary consult if <28-32 weeks, serial bloods every 4-6 hours · term or late preterm (>35-36 weeks): deliver - induction if reassuring, C/S if not

- Follow-up: preterm, stable and bleeding settled: antenatal ward, non-stress test + growth/placental-function ultrasound, periodic bloods by initial values and rebleeding

lectures.name: Approach to the Small Fetus
lectures.title: Approach to the small fetus
lectures.framing: Three labels that sound alike and mean different things: small for gestational age (SGA) is a percentile, low birth weight (LBW) is a weight, intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) is a pathological process, and the first two say nothing about the third. The job is to find the fetus that is IUGR as early as possible, name the cause, then let the Doppler and the gestational age decide delivery.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ SGA is a percentile (<10th), LBW is a weight (<2500 g), IUGR is a process, and an IUGR fetus can be above the 10th percentile. SFH >2-3 cm less than weeks screens; ultrasound EFW confirms. A trisomy is the intrinsic cause; smoking, hypertension and multiples restrict nutrient delivery. Placental insufficiency below the 3rd percentile shows absent EDF and ↓ amniotic fluid, not polyhydramnios. Delivery, not time, is the only way to feed the fetus better.

- Follow-up: frequency set by severity and by NST / Doppler findings

lectures.name: Approach to Preterm Labour
lectures.title: Approach to preterm labour
lectures.framing: Everything turns on where she sits on one line: threatened preterm labour → preterm labour → preterm birth, with membranes intact or ruptured. Each step adds the intervention that buys the next one time: hydrate, then tocolyse to buy 48 hours, spend them on steroids and transfer, and when birth is imminent switch to magnesium and penicillin.
lectures.keypoints: ⚠ Antibiotics in PPROM INCREASE latency (the inherited note had it backwards). Steroids are the one intervention given at every stage; tocolysis needs contractions, magnesium needs an imminent birth, penicillin needs a delivery. Cerclage is for cervical insufficiency before 24 weeks, never for ruptured membranes. Dehydration and UTI mimic TPTL: hydrate and dip the urine before reaching for a tocolytic.

- Treatment / Management: the grid below, in the order the stage demands

- Follow-up: admit for monitoring · ⭐ PPROM < 32 weeks with no intervention: 50% deliver within 48 hours, 75% within 7 days

lectures.framing: Labour is regular uterine contractions causing progressive cervical dilation, and each stage asks the same two questions: what event ends it, and what am I measuring to know it is progressing. The 1st stage is measured on the cervix, the 2nd on the fetus, the 3rd on the placenta, the 4th on the mother.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ true labour = regular contractions causing progressive cervical dilation; Braxton Hicks change nothing at the cervix. Station is measured from the ischial spines, dilation is complete at 10 cm. ⚠ The earliest sign of placental separation is the firm, globular uterus, not the gush of blood. ⚠ In the 4th stage the danger is postpartum hemorrhage on top of a 500 mL autotransfusion, so a cardiac patient needs watching for the ↑ cardiac work.

lectures.title: Abnormal labour and birth
lectures.framing: Every route in this lecture gets a baby out when labour will not do it alone, and each one has a gate. The Bishop score gates induction, a fully dilated cervix with an engaged vertex gates an instrument, a low segment scar gates a trial of labour after cesarean, and in a postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) a firm or an atonic uterus decides the next step.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Uterine atony is the primary cause of PPH, and the rate is rising - so a firm uterus sends you looking for trauma instead. Abnormal FHR is the #1 reason for an operative vaginal delivery and the first sign of a uterine rupture. ⚠ Vacuum cannot rotate; forceps can. A previous C/S for dystocia lowers vaginal birth after cesarean success; a non-recurrent indication (breech) raises it. ⚠ Carboprost in asthma, ergonovine in hypertension.

lectures.name: Hemorrhagic Shock
lectures.title: Hemorrhagic shock
lectures.framing: Shock is cellular hypoxia, and hemorrhagic shock is the hypovolemic kind: lost blood → ↓ preload → ↓ cardiac output. The whole lecture turns on one thing: grade the loss from the vitals, then resuscitate before the vitals agree with you, because the obstetric patient is young, healthy and volume-expanded, so she compensates until she suddenly does not.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Blood pressure is normal through class II (up to 30% loss, ~1500 mL); it falls only in class III, so a normal BP does not exclude shock and tachycardia (> 100, class II) is the first vital to move. ⚠ Do not overlook the young healthy patient: she may surprise you with how much she has lost while still looking well. Bleeding is treated by stopping the bleeding; fluids and blood buy time, and each unit given feeds the coagulopathy arm of the triad.

blocks.lead:
Workup skeleton

- History / recognise: the 8 features of shock: hypotension · tachycardia · oliguria · abnormal mental status · tachypnea · cool, clammy, cyanotic skin · metabolic acidosis · hyperlactatemia

- First moves: airway, breathing, circulation and call for HELP · vitals (heart rate, blood pressure (BP), respiratory rate, O2 saturation) with arterial blood gas / venous blood gas · large-bore intravenous (IV) x 2, crystalloids / colloids · O2 · Foley to urometer (urine output is a vital sign here)

- Investigations: complete blood count · group and screen · partial thromboplastin time / international normalized ratio · fibrinogen · creatinine

- Treatment: blood products (packed red blood cells, platelets, cryoprecipitate, fresh frozen plasma) → consider massive transfusion protocol · identify and address the cause, stop the bleeding · consider ICU (inotropes, central lines)

- Throughout: prevent the lethal triad (below)

blocks.html: Why obstetrics and gynecology is different: the population is young and healthy, and the post-partum woman has a pregnancy-expanded blood volume built for the blood loss of delivery, so she compensates well despite a large loss.

lectures.name: Lactation
lectures.title: Lactation
lectures.framing: Lactation needs three things: prolactin to make milk, oxytocin to eject it, and removal of milk by infant or pump, which must begin by day 3. Nearly every breastfeeding problem is a failure of one of the three, so ask which one broke.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ By day 3 control switches from endocrine to autocrine: milk removal, not hormone, now drives supply, which is why removal must start by day 3 and why poor extraction lowers production. Low supply is the most common reason to stop breastfeeding. Mastitis is treated by continuing to nurse, not by stopping; an abscess needs drainage. Breast size doesn't matter. Alcohol is not a contraindication; smoking and street drugs are to be avoided.

lectures.name: Postpartum Care
lectures.title: Postpartum care
lectures.framing: The puerperium is a return to baseline on a fixed timetable, so the complication is whatever breaks the timetable: blues past 2 weeks, bright red bleeding returning after 24 h, fever on 2 of the first 10 days.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Blues that last more than 2 weeks, or are severe within the first 2 weeks, are postpartum depression. ⚠ EPDS item 10 scored 1-3 at any total is a self-harm risk needing immediate assessment. The puerperal-infection clock excludes the first 24 h, and delayed PPH starts after 24 h. Refer ALL antepartum and postpartum patients to pelvic floor physiotherapy.

lectures.name: Approach to Neonatal Care
lectures.title: Approach to Neonatal Care
lectures.framing: Every newborn is examined within 24 h and kept pink, warm and sweet; the extra care turns on which reserve this baby lacks: heat (no shivering), glucose (glycogen lasts 8-10 h, gluconeogenesis not normal until 2-4 days), or bilirubin clearance.
lectures.keypoints: ⭐ Symptomatic hypoglycemia is a medical emergency: IV dextrose, not a feed (a jittery IDM who cannot latch, glucose 2.3). The GA curves run higher the more mature the baby, so the same TSB can need treatment at 35 weeks and not at 40. ⚠ Sepsis runs through all three: hypoglycemia can be a sign of it, it causes hyperbilirubinemia, and temperature instability is a jaundice risk factor, so consider it in any sick baby.

Neurotoxicity risk factors (act at a lower TSB): < 38 weeks · albumin < 30 · suspected hemolysis · suspected sepsis · hemodynamic or respiratory instability. Rules of 30 (≥ 35 weeks): phototherapy when within 30 μmol/L of the threshold in a baby with these risk factors; stop when > 30 below (≥ 38 weeks) or > 60 below (35-37 weeks).
Phototherapy works three ways: Z → E isomerization (to bile) · cyclization to lumirubin (bile, urine) · oxidation (urine).
